issue.standard_remedy: Qualify a second source and shift volume
issue.summary: High-risk supplier (score 49.2) holds 12% of a category

plan.diagnosis: Unity Components AG represents a concentrated single-source risk with 11.6% category share and USD 710,555 annual spend, scoring 49.2 on risk (elevated) with poor ESG performance (45) and failure class 3. The supplier's below-average resiliency score (57) combined with high category concentration creates supply continuity and compliance exposure across the multi-ERP environment.

remedy_steps.step: Launch dual-sourcing initiative: issue RFI to 3-5 qualified alternative suppliers in the same category to establish technical and commercial viability for 40-50% volume transfer
Negotiate trial orders (10% of current volume, approximately USD 71,000) with top 2 RFI respondents; validate quality, delivery performance, and system integration
Select secondary supplier and execute contract for 40% volume reallocation (USD 284,000 annual run-rate); update all ERP source lists and establish backup approved vendor records
Implement quarterly business reviews with Unity Components AG focused on ESG improvement plan (target score >60) and resiliency enhancements; tie 15% of volume retention to documented progress
Configure risk monitoring alerts across all ERP systems for any supplier exceeding 8% category share; establish automated escalation workflow

plan.expected_impact: Reducing Unity Components AG category concentration from 11.6% to ~7% through USD 284,000 volume shift will mitigate single-source risk exposure by approximately 40% while maintaining competitive tension.
kpis: Category concentration ratio for Unity Components AG (target: <8% from current 11.6%)
Unity Components AG ESG score improvement (target: 45 to >60 within 12 months)
Annual spend with qualified alternatives (target: USD 284,000)
Supply disruption incidents from this category (target: zero events)
risks: Alternative suppliers may lack technical capability or capacity, delaying qualification timeline by 8-12 weeks
Unity Components AG may respond to volume reduction with price increases (estimated 5-8% on remaining USD 426,555 spend)
Multi-ERP source list synchronization failures could result in maverick buying or duplicate POs
Quality issues during supplier transition could disrupt production (estimated 2-3 week exposure window)
Incumbent supplier relationship deterioration may impact service levels on retained 60% volume
erp_actions: SAP: Create secondary source list entries (ME01) for new qualified supplier(s) with 40% quota allocation; maintain Unity Components AG at 60% quota
SAP: Update LFA1/LFB1 vendor master with risk flag and spending limit of USD 60,000/month (monitoring threshold) for Unity Components AG
Oracle EBS: Add approved supplier record and create blanket purchase agreement for secondary source with USD 284,000 annual value
Dynamics 365: Configure vendor category limits and enable workflow approval for any single PO to Unity Components AG exceeding USD 25,000
NetSuite: Establish preferred vendor hierarchy with dual-source logic; set Unity Components AG reorder point triggers to include secondary supplier notification
Coupa: Implement supplier risk score integration (49.2 baseline) with automated alerts for any deterioration >5 points; enable split-PO functionality for category
All systems: Synchronize vendor payment terms to Net 60 for Unity Components AG (leverage for ESG compliance) and Net 45 for new secondary source (incentive)
